headline: Over 200 migrants rescued off Greece coast, mostly from Bangladesh and Sudan
summary: Greek authorities rescued 202 migrants traveling from Libya to Crete, including dozens of Bangladeshi nationals.
details: Greek authorities have rescued at least 202 irregular migrants who arrived on the shores of Crete in several boat trips within 48 hours.
The rescued individuals are primarily citizens of Bangladesh and Sudan, with some Egyptian nationals also among them.
In one trip, 112 migrants arrived in two boats. One boat carried 56 people, including 31 Sudanese and 25 Bangladeshis. The second boat carried 56 people, including 47 Bangladeshis and 9 Egyptians.
Another boat carrying 40 migrants was spotted by a Frontex aircraft and brought to Ierapetra port by a coast guard patrol vessel and a fishing boat.
All rescued migrants have been moved to a temporary shelter in the port of Heraklion, where they are undergoing identity verification.
Local authorities and migrant reception centers on the island of Crete are facing increased pressure due to the continuous influx of migrants from Libya.
caption:
Over 200 migrants, including dozens of Bangladeshis, were rescued off the coast of Greece after crossing the Mediterranean from Libya.

Greek authorities have rescued at least 202 irregular migrants who arrived on the shores of Crete in several boat trips within 48 hours.

The rescued individuals are primarily citizens of Bangladesh and Sudan, with some Egyptian nationals also among them.

In one trip, 112 migrants arrived in two boats. One boat carried 56 people, including 31 Sudanese and 25 Bangladeshis. The second boat carried 56 people, including 47 Bangladeshis and 9 Egyptians.

Another boat carrying 40 migrants was spotted by a Frontex aircraft and brought to Ierapetra port by a coast guard patrol vessel and a fishing boat.

All rescued migrants have been moved to a temporary shelter in the port of Heraklion, where they are undergoing identity verification.

Local authorities and migrant reception centers on the island of Crete are facing increased pressure due to the continuous influx of migrants from Libya.

headline: AI model creates 16 new viruses after DNA training
summary: Stanford University researchers used a generative AI model called 'Evo' to design genetic blueprints for viruses that do not exist in nature.
details: Scientists at Stanford University trained a generative AI model named 'Evo' on millions of genomes to understand how viruses evolve. Using this knowledge, the AI designed thousands of new genetic blueprints, 16 of which were successfully created in a lab and found to be functional viruses capable of infecting bacteria.

The researchers emphasized that the AI did not use genetic data from human pathogens, meaning these newly created viruses cannot infect humans. The study, published in the 'Science' journal, notes that these are entirely new genetic designs rather than mere imitations of existing viruses.

While the breakthrough offers potential medical benefits, such as creating targeted viruses to fight antibiotic-resistant bacteria, it has sparked significant biosecurity concerns. Experts warn that similar technology could be misused to create dangerous biological weapons or more lethal pathogens.

Biosecurity specialists from the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security have called for strict laws and regulatory frameworks to prevent the misuse of generative AI in biology. They argue that such technology could potentially be used to design more contagious or deadly versions of existing viruses.

In response to these risks, several major AI companies have formed the 'Frontier Model Forum' to research safety standards and prevent the misuse of advanced AI models. Some scientists believe that controlling access to genetic data could significantly reduce the risk of creating biological weapons.
